newsitem.title: USA: DSP sees Q2 results below Q1.
newsitem.headline: DSP sees Q2 results below Q1.

text.p: DSP Communications Inc said Wednesday it expects earnings and revenues for its second quarter will be materially below first quarter levels.
The company said in a statement that second quarter production will be reduced due to the phase-out of DSP's existing chip sets as its customers transition to new models.
"The second quarter of 1997 is a transition quarter for our personal digital cellular customers and for our company," said President and Chief Executive Officer Nathan Hod.
DSP said that toward the end of the first quarter its customers said they were designing new cellular telephone models which will use DSP's next generation chip sets.

The company expects these new models will be introduced during the third quarter adding that it believes the new personal digital cellular models will improve its customers' market share during the second half of 1997.

DSP posted first quarter profits of $6.1 million, or $0.13 a share compared to $3.6 million, or $0.09 a share in the comparable year-ago period. Revenues were $20.3 million, up from 17.3 million in the year-ago period.
